source_title: Histoire de la Revolution Francaise, tome dixieme, neuvieme edition
event_text: These arrangements, which had won the admiration of all the critics, were put into execution on 3 Vendemiaire, Year VIII (25 September 1799), at five in the morning. Preparations for the crossing had been made near the village of Dietikon with extraordinary care and secrecy. Boats had been dragged by hand and hidden in the woods. By morning they were afloat, and the troops were silently drawn up on the bank. General Foy, later distinguished as an orator, commanded the artillery in this memorable battle; he positioned several batteries to protect the crossing. Six hundred men boldly embarked and reached the opposite bank. They immediately attacked and scattered the enemy skirmishers. Korsakoff had stationed three battalions with artillery there, on the plateau of Closter-Fahr. Our artillery, skilfully directed, soon silenced the Russian guns and protected the successive crossings of our advance guard. When General Gazan had assembled sufficient reinforcements with the six hundred men who had crossed first, he advanced against the three Russian battalions guarding Closter-Fahr. They had established themselves in a wood and defended it bravely. Gazan surrounded them and had to kill almost every last man to dislodge them. Once these three battalions had been destroyed, the bridge was laid. The rest of Lorge's division and part of Mesnard's division crossed the Limmat: fifteen thousand men had been brought across the river. Bontemps's brigade was stationed at Regensdorf to face Durasof should he move up from the lower Limmat. The main body, directed by chief of staff Oudinot, moved upstream along the Limmat to reach the rear of Zurich.
source_text: Ces dispositions, qui ont fait l'admiration de tous les critiques, furent mises à exécution le 3 vendémiaire an VIII (25 septembre 1799), à cinq heures du matin. Les apprêts du passage avaient été faits près du village de Dietikon, avec un soin et un secret extraordinaires. Des barques avaient été traînées à bras, et cachées dans les bois. Dès le matin, elles étaient à flot, et les troupes étaient rangées en silence sur la rive. Le général Foy, illustré depuis comme orateur, commandait l'artillerie à cette immortelle bataille; il disposa plusieurs batteries de manière à protéger le passage. Six cents hommes s'embarquèrent hardiment, et arrivèrent sur l'autre rive. Sur-le-champ ils fondirent sur les tirailleurs ennemis, et les dispersèrent. Korsakoff avait mis là, sur le plateau de Closter-Fahr, trois bataillons avec du canon. Notre artillerie, supérieurement dirigée, éteignit bientôt les feux de l'artillerie russe, et protégea le passage successif de notre avant-garde. Lorsque le général Gazan eut réuni aux six cents hommes qui avaient passé les premiers un renfort suffisant, il marcha sur les trois bataillons russes qui gardaient Closter-Fahr. Ceux-ci s'étaient logés dans un bois, et s'y défendirent bravement. Gazan les enveloppa, et fut obligé de tuer presque jusqu'au dernier homme pour les déloger. Ces trois bataillons détruits, le pont fut jeté. Le reste de la division Lorge et partie de la division Mesnard passèrent la Limmat: c'étaient quinze mille hommes portés au-delà de la rivière. La brigade Bontemps fut placée à Regensdorf, pour faire face à Durasof, s'il voulait remonter de la Basse-Limmat. Le gros des troupes, dirigé par le chef d'état-major Oudinot, remonta la Limmat, pour se porter sur les derrières de Zurich.
source_section: CHAPITRE XVIII; paragraph beginning: Ces dispositions, qui ont fait l'admiration de tous les critiques, furent mises à exécution le 3 vendémiaire an VIII (25 septembre 1799), à cinq heures du matin.
target_question: Immediately after their initial boat crossing, where did the first six hundred French soldiers land, before Gazan assembled further reinforcements?
target_time: immediately after initial crossing, before reinforcements
annotation_caution: Localize the receiving bank, not Dietikon's village centre, the departure bank, or the later bridge. Several bank segments may fit; do not copy the red crossing arrow. Mark ambiguous if text and geography do not identify a sufficiently constrained area.

source_title: Histoire de la Revolution Francaise, tome dixieme, neuvieme edition
event_text: Once this part of the operation was completed, Massena personally returned to the other bank of the Limmat to oversee the movements of his wings. On the lower Limmat, Mesnard had so thoroughly deceived Durasof with his demonstrations that the latter had moved to the bank and opened fire with all his guns. On his right, Mortier had advanced towards Zurich by way of Wollishofen, but had encountered Korsakoff's main force, positioned, as already stated, in front of the Limmat, and had been compelled to fall back. Arriving at that moment, Massena set Klein's division, which was at Altstetten, in motion. Humbert, at the head of his four thousand grenadiers, marched on Zurich and restored the battle. Mortier renewed his attacks, and the Russians were thus confined within Zurich.
source_text: Cette partie de l'opération achevée, Masséna se reporta de sa personne sur l'autre rive de la Limmat, pour veiller au mouvement de ses ailes. Vers la Basse-Limmat, Mesnard avait si bien trompé Durasof par ses démonstrations, que celui-ci s'était porté sur la rive, où il déployait tous ses feux. A sa droite, Mortier s'était avancé sur Zurich par Wollishofen, mais il y avait rencontré la masse de Korsakoff, posté, comme on l'a dit, en avant de la Limmat, et avait été obligé de se replier. Masséna arrivant dans cet instant ébranla la division Klein, qui était à Altstetten. Humbert, à la tête de ses quatre mille grenadiers, marcha sur Zurich, et rétablit le combat. Mortier renouvela ses attaques, et on parvint à renfermer ainsi les Russes dans Zurich.
source_section: CHAPITRE XVIII; paragraph beginning: Cette partie de l'opération achevée, Masséna se reporta de sa personne sur l'autre rive de la Limmat, pour veiller au mouvement de ses ailes.
target_question: Where was Klein's division stationed immediately before Massena set it in motion, rather than where Humbert subsequently marched?
target_time: immediately before Massena set the division in motion
annotation_caution: Explicit-place control with a temporal distinction. The target is the pre-movement locality, not Zurich or Mortier's route. The text does not support an exact military formation footprint.

source_title: Histoire de la Revolution Francaise, tome dixieme, neuvieme edition
event_text: Meanwhile, Korsakoff, troubled by hearing cannon fire in his rear, had sent some battalions back across the Limmat, but these weak reinforcements had been of no use. Oudinot, with his fifteen thousand men, continued moving upstream along the Limmat. He had captured the small camp at Hong, as well as the heights behind Zurich, and had seized the main road to Vintherthur, which led into Germany and was the only route by which the Russians could retreat.
source_text: Pendant ce temps, Korsakoff, chagriné d'entendre du canon sur ses derrières, avait reporté quelques bataillons au-delà de la Limmat; mais ces faibles secours avaient été inutiles. Oudinot, avec ses quinze mille hommes, continuait à remonter la Limmat. Il avait enlevé le petit camp placé à Hong, ainsi que les hauteurs qui sont sur les derrières de Zurich, et s'était emparé de la grande route de Vintherthur, qui donne issue en Allemagne, et la seule par laquelle les Russes pussent se retirer.
source_section: CHAPITRE XVIII; paragraph beginning: Pendant ce temps, Korsakoff, chagriné d'entendre du canon sur ses derrières, avait reporté quelques bataillons au-delà de la Limmat; mais ces faibles secours avaient été inutiles.
target_question: Which high-ground area had Oudinot captured during his upstream advance, distinct from the small camp and the main road also mentioned?
annotation_caution: Behind Zurich depends on the operational viewpoint; it is not automatically geographic north. Several heights may fit. Use terrain, river and approach context, not troop arrows alone. Mark ambiguous if the specific high-ground area cannot be distinguished.
